title: Noise decomposition of a coordinate restriction
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, $f\colon\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb{R}$, $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$, $b\in\{0,1\}$, and $x\in\{0,1\}^n$. Write $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, $a_f(x)=\tfrac12(f(x,0)+f(x,1))$, $d_f(x)=\tfrac12(f(x,0)-f(x,1))$, and $\sigma(0)=1$, $\sigma(1)=-1$. Applying the noise operator on the first $n$ coordinates gives $(T_\rho f_b)(x)=(T_\rho a_f)(x)+\sigma(b)(T_\rho d_f)(x)$.
replaced: Let $T_\rho$ denote Boolean noise with real correlation $\rho$, whose Fourier multiplier on a set of size $k$ is $\rho^k$. For $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, put $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, $a_f=(f_0+f_1)/2$, and $d_f=(f_0-f_1)/2$, and let $s_0=1$, $s_1=-1$. For every $x,b$ and real $\rho$, $(T_\rho f_b)(x)=(T_\rho a_f)(x)+s_b(T_\rho d_f)(x)$, where noise on the right acts on the first $n$ coordinates.
